meta.scene_summary: We're busy building the future with robot dogs and AI, while the bill for the electricity and the consequences of our own surveillance tools is finally coming due.

cooking.headline: Anthropic just proved that 'National Security' isn't a get-out-of-court-free card
cooking.summary: The Pentagon tried to use national security as a vague excuse to block Anthropic from certain government contracts, but a judge wasn't buying it. It turns out that even the military has to follow the rules of procurement instead of just pulling the 'top secret' card when they don't like a vendor.
cooking.plain_english: A judge ruled that the Pentagon improperly used national security concerns to restrict Anthropic from competing for government contracts.

cooking.headline: Debian decides to let AI help write the code that keeps the world running
cooking.summary: Debian is officially allowing generative AI in its codebase, effectively giving the world's most stable operating system a caffeine-addicted intern. It's the ultimate test of whether 'responsible use' can survive the pressure of a million packages waiting to be merged.
cooking.plain_english: The Debian project has updated its rules to permit the use of artificial intelligence tools in the development and maintenance of its software.

cooking.headline: ICE is buying robot dogs, because human employees weren't dystopian enough
cooking.summary: Federal agencies are spending millions to upgrade their patrol game with Boston Dynamics' mechanical canines. It's the ultimate group project where the hardware is elite, but the ethics committee clearly skipped the sprint planning meeting.

cooking.headline: LibreOffice 26.8 is officially an AI-free zone for the paranoid and the productive.
cooking.summary: While everyone else is busy shoving LLMs into their calculators and toasters, LibreOffice decided that being offline is the new premium feature. It is refreshing to use software that doesn't try to hallucinate your spreadsheet formulas while you're just trying to balance a budget.
cooking.plain_english: The latest version of the LibreOffice software suite prioritizes local file storage and contains no artificial intelligence features.

cooking.headline: Open-source guardrails so your AI doesn't hallucinate a felony
cooking.summary: Conduct provides guardrails for LLM tool calls, finally acknowledging that giving an AI access to your system is like handing a toddler the keys to a forklift. It's a necessary safety layer for when your model decides that 'delete all files' is the logical solution to a minor syntax error.
cooking.plain_english: This tool provides security controls for AI models to ensure they perform only authorized actions when using software tools.

cooking.headline: SteamOS 3.9.0 is here to make your handheld feel like a real PC
cooking.summary: Valve is pushing another SteamOS update, proving they are the only company that actually enjoys maintaining a Linux distro for gamers. It's nice to see a handheld get more love than my actual workstation gets from my IT department.
cooking.plain_english: Valve has released a new preview version of its Linux-based operating system for the Steam Deck and other handheld gaming devices.

cooked.headline: Data centers are realizing that electricity isn't free or infinite
cooked.summary: The AI boom is hitting a massive wall because data centers are consuming so much power that they are literally running out of juice. It's like throwing a massive house party and realizing you forgot to check if your apartment's breaker box can actually handle the load.
cooked.plain_english: Data centers are struggling to secure enough electricity to support the rapid growth of AI infrastructure and computing demands.

cooked.headline: The irony of a surveillance CEO getting their own home address doxxed
cooked.summary: The CEO of a company that builds license-plate-tracking cameras for police just found out what it's like to be on the other side of the lens. Apparently, privacy is a great feature for everyone except the person selling the surveillance software.
cooked.plain_english: The residential address of the CEO of Flock Safety was shared publicly online following a backlash against the company's surveillance technology.

cooked.headline: When the police department's surveillance tool becomes a stalker's side quest
cooked.summary: A police officer used a license plate tracking system to monitor his ex-girlfriend over 2,000 times. It turns out that building a database of everyone's movements is a great feature, unless the person holding the keys is a creep.
cooked.plain_english: A law enforcement officer was arrested for repeatedly misusing a vehicle tracking system to monitor a former partner.

cooked.headline: The 9th Circuit just reminded Kalshi that betting on elections is still a felony in some neighborhoods.
cooked.summary: Kalshi really thought they could gamify democracy until the courts decided that betting on the government is a bit too spicy for public consumption. It turns out that treating the Senate like a sportsbook might actually land you in a legal side quest you didn't want.
cooked.plain_english: A federal court has allowed states to continue legal efforts to block a platform from offering financial bets on political election results.
